stories.title: Trump confirms he secretly switched planes over threat
stories.summary: Donald Trump has confirmed that he secretly switched planes because of a threat to his life, after the Washington Post reported the US president was smuggled out of Air Force One to a different aircraft on a catering truck. "They wanted me to go in a different flight, a different plane - equal safety, but they wanted me to do it, so I do it," Mr Trump told reporters, adding "I do what they say". "I guess there was a threat out there. I didn't really ask too much about it," he said. The newspaper reported on Monday that the secret operation reportedly smuggled Mr Trump off Air Force One before the plane departed, still carrying journalists and top aides who remained at apparent risk of an Iranian strike.

stories.title: Assault, harassment and stalking top calls to victim line
stories.summary: Almost one in every two crime-related contacts received by Ireland's national victims' support service last year related to assault, harassment or stalking. The Crime Victims Helpline (CVH) supported 5,902 contacts in 2025, and provided 3,268 referrals to specialist victim support, criminal justice and community services. Founded just over 20 years ago, the helpline provides information and support to victims of crime in Ireland. The number of contacts supported by the charity last year fell by almost 1,000 contacts (967) compared to the previous year.

stories.title: Over half a million Irish passports issued this year
stories.summary: Holidaymakers have been urged to check their passport expiry dates to ensure travel plans go smoothly during the remainder of the busy summer season. Figures from the Department of Foreign Affairs showed over half a million Irish passports were issued in the first half of 2026. On the island of Ireland, 367,471 passports were issued in total. Over 50,000 passports were issued in the six counties of Northern Ireland, of which Antrim, on 17,986, saw the third-highest figure across all 32 counties.

It is forecast to have revenues of €280m this year, with its earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation forecast to reach €90m. It said its business would be "highly complementary" to its Advnsys subsidiary, which designs and builds data centre facilities.

stories.title: Russia uses N Korean missiles in deadly attack - Zelensky
stories.summary: Russian forces killed six people early today in an attack on the southeastern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia that involved North Korean ballistic missiles, President Volodymyr Zelensky said. Six others were killed overnight in the Ukrainian regions of Dnipropetrovsk and Donetsk, and a Russian attack on Kyiv caused fires in the capital, Ukrainian officials said. Regional governor Ivan Fedorov posted photos online showing buildings and vehicles ablaze in Zaporizhzhia, where officials said 20 people had also been wounded. "The city was hit by North Korean ballistic missiles, Zircons (anti-ship missiles) and KABs (precision-guided aerial bombs)," Mr Zelensky wrote on Telegram.

stories.summary: Shamrock Rovers are closing in on European group stage football for the fourth time this decade, something they deserve massive credit for. The Hoops take a 3-1 to Albania on Thursday in their third round Europa League qualifier, where progress will ensure them to league phase in the Conference League, as a minimum. But manager Stephen Bradley spoke last year of what progress would look like after the club claimed the domestic double, and he specifically mentioned reaching the Europa League outright. It means losing by less than two goals against Egnatia, with Norwegian outfit Lillestrom standing between them and a place in the league phase of Europe's mid-tier club competition.

Galway were beaten 2-14 to 0-19 by Cork in Croke Park on Sunday but won the All-Ireland final in 2025 and 2019. The GAA has a fund of €150,000 which is available to the All-Ireland senior football and hurling finalists annually to go towards a holiday at the end of the season but they same pool of money does not exist in camogie. "I think Cork and Galway have been unbelievable the last three years and they've brought camogie to a different level. Them girls, when we won the All-Ireland last year, we were out fundraising. The same when we won the All-Ireland in '19. Going around to club matches with buckets asking people for fivers, asking people for tenners, asking people for change," Murray said after the match.

stories.title: Carney: Irish fans will embrace 'relentless' rugby league
stories.summary: Former rugby league star Brian Carney is confident the Irish sporting public will embrace next year's historic Super League fixtures at the RDS. Warrington Wolves and Wigan Warriors will face off at the newly redeveloped Laya Arena in Dublin on Saturday 24 April 2027, with St Helens taking on Hull FC at the same venue the next day. It is not an unprecedented move. While it will be the first time Super League games have been held in this country, Warrington and Wigan previously met at Shelbourne Park back in 1934, while Wigan returned to the capital in 1995 to face Leeds in a Charity Shield fixture. Corkman Carney forged a highly distinguished career in rugby league, lining out for Hull, Wigan Warriors, Newcastle Knights (in Australia) and Warrington Wolves. He also represented Munster in rugby union, won four caps for Ireland and played international rugby sevens.

stories.title: How Glee helped me find my voice - and inspired a new musical
stories.summary: A Glee-obsessed teenager at an all-boys school, Conor Burke found refuge in music while navigating bullying, the closet, and a life far less colourful than his favourite TV show... Conor introduces his joyful new musical about hope, resilience, and finding your voice - even when the world begs you to stop singing - coming to this year's Dublin Fringe Festival. There is a moment in the fourth episode of the juggernaut television show Glee, when Kurt Hummel, the effeminate and theatrical boy soprano, comes out of the closet to his blue-collar, pragmatic, ultra-masculine father. It is a tense moment for the young boy, who, for all intents and purposes, had barely even acknowledged his identity to himself. A television show daring to address a relatively taboo topic such as teenage homosexuality on network television in 2009 was daring - and the characters involved, as well as the audience watching, knew it.

stories.title: Rose of Tralee: "It's like a fever dream to be in it"
stories.summary: Presenters Dáithí Ó Sé and Kathryn Thomas entered a garden full of roses today, launching the 66th Rose of Tralee competition on the beautiful grounds of Saint Helen's Hotel in Co. Dublin. Celebrating Irish identity in its many forms, the five-day festival has become a platform for the talents, interests and ambitions of modern women. This year, the contestants seem to be particularly open, giving insights into their lives in terms of their health, their advocacy work, their grief, and the matters that drive them. The result is a variety of causes being platformed by the 32 contestants. Cork Rose Lexi Linnane hopes to raise awareness of strokes, having lost her mother three years ago; Tipperary Rose Fiona Kennedy is highlighting the issue of arthritis in young people, following her diagnosis at 14; and Westmeath Rose Caoilfhinn Ní Choiligh hopes to create a community for those living with alopecia, having experienced hair loss for the last 10 years herself.

stories.title: New attacks on shipping as Iran talks hit fresh impasse
stories.summary: The US and Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis reported separate attacks on shipping as prospects for ending the Iran war appeared to dim, with Tehran saying the Strait of Hormuz would remain closed unless Washington accepts its conditions. The attacks, in the Gulf of ⁠Oman leading to the strait and at the entrance to the Red Sea, both vital chokepoints for global oil supplies, come as the war shows no signs of ending despite repeated assertions from US President Donald Trump of a deal being imminent. Oil prices gained and global shares retreated amid renewed pessimism about a quick end to the conflict. Brent crude futures climbed 1.4% to settle at $88.91 (€77) per barrel and US crude rose 1.3% to $83.20 (€72).

stories.title: NI minister reveals death threat after culling of 51 cows
stories.summary: Northern Ireland's Agriculture Minister Andrew Muir has said he received a threat that he will be shot following controversy over the culling of 51 cows in Co Tyrone. During an emergency meeting of Stormont's Agriculture Committee, the minister was told that he had "lost all credibility" and that his department had presided over an "animal welfare scandal" after the cows were shot in fields. The minister urged MLAs to temper their language after the committee heard a claim that the public believes that there had been a "shoot to kill" approach over the animals. The Department of Agriculture, Environment and Rural Affairs’ (Daera) Humane Slaughter Team carried out the cull of the cattle on land near Fivemiletown in June.

stories.title: Thai PM suspends gun licences after school shooting
stories.summary: Thailand's prime minister said he had suspended firearms licences after last week's deadly school shooting, as the bodies of the teenage assailant and the grandparents he killed were cremated. Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul said he had ordered the interior ministry and police to stop issuing licences to possess, purchase and carry firearms, and called for "tighter controls and decisive penalties". On Friday, a 14-year-old boy shot dead the grandparents who raised him at their home in Nonthaburi, north of Bangkok, before killing six others at his school and then turning the gun on himself. The white caskets of the couple were laid out at the Tem Rak Samakkhi Buddhist temple, alongside their portraits, ahead of their cremation capping a funeral lasting several days.

stories.title: Cecelia Ahern on returning to romance and writing books for kids
stories.summary: Bestselling author Cecelia Ahern talks to Claire O'Mahony about returning to romance, creating a children's heroine inspired by her daughter, and why she still believes in the impossible. It is, perhaps, the closest Cecelia Ahern comes to explaining the thread that runs through everything she writes, and she has always been drawn to stories that ask readers to suspend disbelief. More than 20 years after PS, I Love You introduced her to millions of readers, that instinct is still strong. This summer, however, she is taking it in two very different directions. Within weeks of each other, she is publishing Love Unlocked, her first full romance in years, and Detective Thingy Majiggy, the first in a new children's series inspired by bedtime reading with her youngest daughter, Blossom, aged 6 – she also has two other children, a daughter Robin and son Sonny who are in their teens. The children's novel began, she says, in the most ordinary of ways. "I think it was reading every night with my daughter," the 44-year-old author says. "I had done it with all of my children who are now teenagers, but I just felt like I'd been engrossed in that world myself with my daughter. Night after night reading books; and she's so into these stories. I had ideas that I was like, 'Yeah, this is the time.'"

stories.title: Parking fee revenue at hospitals doubles over four years
stories.summary: Revenue generated by parking fees at public hospitals has more than doubled over a four-year period. A breakdown provided by the HSE shows that Irish people spent a record €17.76m on car park charges at public and voluntary hospitals in 2025 compared to €7.39m in 2021, representing a 140% increase over a four-year period. The rising figure comes despite a commitment in the Programme for Government last year to "explore further ways to reduce hospital car parking charges". Monies gathered by public and voluntary hospitals from parking fees increased in each subsequent year after 2021, going from €10.61m in 2022 to €13.46m in 2023 and €16.18m in 2024.

stories.title: IOC wants regular monitoring of athletes' mental health
stories.summary: Sports bodies should prioritise routine screening and regular monitoring of elite athletes' mental health, the International Olympic Committee has reported. The IOC says fostering good mental health and wellbeing must be done across the board with the timing of support critical. A consensus statement from the IOC states screening and monitoring mental health should be done at predefined points and after significant events, and also address training and competition factors. "While recognition of overt mental health disorders in elite athletes remains essential, situating athlete wellbeing within a dynamic continuum offers an additional framework for understanding the spectrum of psychological functioning in this population," said the IOC in a statement published online in the British Journal of Sports Medicine.

They were well beaten by Westmeath in their Leinster Championship opener, before a Tailteann Cup defeat to Fermanagh. They kept things going with a win over Clare before eventual finalists Down ended their summer.
